The SNARE held half of 250-500 Hz wherever it plays two and four, and the kick most of the rest. Every other song on the album that uses this kit cuts its drums' bus at 400 Hz; this one alone did not. note:
v13, PALETTE, THE THUMBPRINT IS LEFT BY THUMBS: in 'thumbprint' the clean guitar (ct-clean, a staple of six songs on this record) hands its answer to a THUMB PIANO (the library's kalimba, on no other song; two new tracks, tines-left and tines-right, 40 notes). LISTEN FOR 1:49.6–2:17.0, the quiet centre: a wordless voice calls with the four notes and the answer reads them from the other end; nothing else plays until two toms join at 2:03.8. The answer is now plucked tines, two octaves above the guitar's notes, where a kalimba lives (A flat 4 to E flat 5): it was an octave under the voice and is an octave over it, and where the voice climbs for two strips (2:06–2:11.5) they share an octave. AND IT IS PLAYED AS THE INSTRUMENT IS, with two thumbs: a kalimba's tines alternate left and right as they rise, so A flat and B are the left thumb's and A and E flat the right's, a track to a thumb, 0.4 either side of centre. The tune read forwards is therefore left, left, right, right, and read backwards right, right, left, left: turning the strip over swaps the hands, which is the song. Its other thumb is the bass player's (from 1:06, on its card); this section's name was waiting for one. THE SWAP: the same 40 notes at the same times, lengths and velocities; the clean guitar still opens the song, rings the fold's F (2:26–2:32) and closes the page. Nothing else changed.
WHAT I MEASURED (raw windows on seed 0, then full renders on seeds 0 and 11). FIRST BENCH, not kept: the same notes at the guitar's own pitch. A kalimba down there is nearly a pure tone at 104–156 Hz, a soft bass and not a tine, and at the first gain it stood 20 dB over the guitar. An octave up it sat in the voice's own octave. KEPT, two octaves up: alone it is within 1.1 dB of the guitar it replaces (K, first 150 ms of each note) and the voice stands 8.6 dB over it where it stood 8.3 over the guitar. Every note's strongest line is its written pitch (415.6, 440.2, 493.7, 622.2 Hz). The library's tine overtone is faint (20 to 26 dB under the fundamental in a note's first 30 ms), so it is lifted 8 dB here (12 to 18 under). Each thumb's notes lean 3.6 and 4.7 dB toward its side. COST: the section loses the guitar's pick: -1.2 dB at 2–4 kHz and -2.7 at 4–8 kHz; every band under 2 kHz is within 0.6 dB, and the section reads -18.05 -> -18.17 LUFS mastered on seed 0 and -18.07 -> -18.02 on seed 11. LOUDNESS TARGET -10.143 (was -10.15): at the old target every other bar came out 0.004 to 0.010 dB quieter; now +0.004 / -0.004. Everything outside the section is unchanged, the three cards' four excerpts included (-69.7 dB or lower against v12 on both seeds); the first two seconds of 'raised' differ only by what rings into them (-43 dB).
SCORES 0/11: 97.718/97.807 -> 98.020/98.072. All of the rise is the spectrum term (87.1 -> 89.6): its worst band, 83 Hz, reads 0.6 dB less short now that the answer's energy sits higher. That is the scorer's arithmetic, not a verdict on the swap. -10.2 LUFS, -1.28 dBTP.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether this kalimba reads as a thumb piano or as a soft synth blip (its overtone is quiet even lifted); whether the answer above the voice is better than the answer below it, which gave the section its only low notes before the toms; whether two thumbs 0.4 apart are heard as two hands at all.

v16, THE PAGE IS TURNED OVER (section w7, 2:55.4-3:06.3, four strips of 'turn over'; 24 guitar chords repitched and two crashes added; nothing else in the song changes). THE WINDOW was the song's most static (the map: motion 0.006, 'nothing enters in it'): since v15, on Harry's answer ('Prefer both heavy'), 'turn over' is two heavy guitars reading the strip from opposite ends for 33 seconds, changing chairs on every strip, on one harmony until the move to C. Both hands stay heavy. WHAT IS NEW: the song reads its strip from both ends; it had never turned it upside down. After the first pair of strips the page is turned top to bottom for two pairs: every open chord stands as far BELOW the low F as it stood above it, brought up an octave so it stays on the neck. A flat (a minor third up) becomes D (a minor third down); G flat (a semitone up) becomes E (a semitone down); C (a fifth up) becomes B flat (a fifth down). The rhythm, the palm strokes on the low F, the chairs, the bass's F and the kit are as written. What turns is the colour: F, A flat, G flat, C is the dark side of F; F, D, E, B flat is its bright side. Where the two hands meet (ticks 3 and 15 of each strip) they made A flat major seventh over the bass's F; turned over they make B flat major seventh over it. Then the page is turned back for the last pair on F, whose closing C is left ringing and becomes the ground (v12, untouched), and the section ends on C as before. So 'turn over' is now four things in 33 seconds: the strip, its other side, the strip again, and the strip on C. A crash marks each turn of the page; the first falls on a bar line. LISTEN FOR 2:55.4: the crash, and the same riff with the same hits in a major colour, the two guitars still trading sides; 3:06.3: the crash and the dark strip back; 3:11.8 up to C. MEASURED (finished, seeds 0/11): the four turned strips read -13.0 -> -13.0 and -12.8 -> -12.9 K; the pair alone, raw, -27.9 K before and after. Against the eleven records those strips read +1.5 at 250-500 Hz where they read +1.0 (D and E lie higher than A flat and G flat); every other band within 0.3 dB. THE CHANGE IS LOCAL: outside 2:55.4-3:11.8 the song matches v15 with residual -72 dB (seed 0) and -56 (seed 11), gain within 0.015 dB; the two strips after the turn differ at -30 dB (the second crash and the turned chords' tails). The loudness target is not moved. SCORES 0/11: 98.620 / 98.894 (v15 98.607 / 98.851). -10.3 LUFS, -1.28 dBTP. --without-turned-page gives v15 byte for byte; all 14 older switches give what they gave. HARRY'S ANSWERS: 'Prefer both heavy' was built in v15 and holds here; 'Keep the pops' and 'I can follow both' are the song as it stands. WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether eleven seconds of major colour in this song is the other side of the page or a wrong turn; whether E against the low F's palm strokes bites like the G flat it mirrors (it is the same semitone, below instead of above) or sours; whether the crashes are wanted. No card. Not heard by me.
